prize_parts.citation: For the development of dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cells, in which molecular dyes on mesoporous oxide films convert light to electricity.

statement.case_for: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel cell is a materials-chemistry achievement where a designed architecture, a mesoporous nanocrystalline oxide with a molecular sensitizer and a redox mediator, sets the function. It created molecular photovoltaics and a generation of dyes, electrolytes and interface concepts, and it is the direct lineage into perovskite photovoltaics. More than thirty years of independent confirmation and niche commercial use mean there is no maturity question, and the attribution is clean: the origin paper and the sustained development program point to two people. A prize here would also recognize an enabling architecture, not a single device record.
statement.case_against: Dye-sensitized cells never reached the efficiency or cost that was promised and have been displaced by perovskites and silicon, so a prize may look like honoring a superseded technology. Its impact on practice is less than that of base editing or degraders, and several colleagues weigh clinical and biomedical consequence heavily. Hagfeldt's later contributions are real and a two-person cut could be argued to under-credit the field.

responses.point: Base editing (B024) is a clear, explainable principle with a rich chain from mechanism to clinical trials, and the Liu-Komor-Gaudelli configuration follows the primary record.
responses.response: I agree the chemistry is real and the Liu-led attribution is persuasive, and I rank it as my fallback. My reservations are two. The 2020 CRISPR prize makes this the second genome-editing recognition in six years, and the Kondo and Nishida priority question, which you also flag, is not settled by calling the Liu papers the cleaner story. I would ask for the evidence on that before treating the trio as uncontested. Opening support is also not scientific merit, and a tool built on a protein platform already honored sits in tension with a definitive, self-contained chemical advance.

responses.point: Nitrogenase (B038) is a central problem of biological energy conversion, with structural work on the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor, including the carbide, plus kinetic mechanism work.
responses.response: As a structural chemist I respect the cofactor structure and the carbide, which was a hard crystallographic result. My concern is that the prize would have to bundle structure with a turnover mechanism you yourself call unresolved, and the credit split among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is hard to cut at three. Structure alone answers what the cofactor is, not how it reduces N2. I would support it if the citation is limited to the structure, but I think B025 offers a cleaner configuration.

responses.point: Perovskite absorbers (B060) are a real materials game-changer, but stability, lead toxicity and scale-up argue for waiting.
responses.response: I share your maturity concern, and that is why B060 is not my first choice. I would add that the structural origin of defect tolerance and the degradation pathways are still debated, so the discovery is not settled even at the crystal-structure level. The lineage runs from the dye-sensitized cell, so recognizing B025 first respects the chronology and avoids a priority fight among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Kanatzidis. I do not agree that waiting is costless, because the three-person limit will keep shrinking the credit for perovskites.

responses.point: Base editors turn a biological tool into a chemically defined editing reagent, are in clinical use for sickle cell disease, and change what researchers and clinicians can do.
responses.response: Clinical use is a strong argument for impact, and I do not dismiss it. But I would separate an engineered protein fusion built on Cas9 from a self-contained chemical concept. Prime editing (B011) overlaps with Liu's program, and you note that a combined citation may be needed, so this candidate is less sharply bounded than the DSSC. I also ask how much the deaminase evolution, which is the original chemistry, is carried by the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the dye-sensitized cell as a completed achievement or as superseded by perovskites.
Whether two names (Grätzel, O'Regan) is the right cut or Hagfeldt should be considered, and I have not verified the relative credit from the primary papers.
Whether the CRISPR-adjacent B024 will gather enough support that B025 cannot compete, and the Kondo and Nishida priority question.
Whether a perovskite prize would be more compelling to colleagues once stability data are weighed.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, who ranks B038 first, and my own work in porous and framework materials is near but not part of any shortlisted candidate; none of the credited names is a known collaborator or mentor.
